title: Build-Measure-Learn Loop
hook: The team that learns every week will beat the team that learns every month. Every time.
statement: Build something, measure what people actually do, then decide whether to change course or keep going.
explainer: Learning compounds. Lots of startups stay busy shipping without learning anything real. The point of every loop is one honest lesson, and the faster you loop, the more lessons stack up.
sop: Build the smallest experiment you can.
Measure what people do, not what they say.
Write down what turned out to be true.
Run the next loop faster than the last.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Cycle Speed 7, Hypothesis Quality 6. (7 + 6) ÷ 2 = 6.5. Higher means you're stacking real knowledge fast. Lower means you're moving slowly or testing ideas too vague to give a clear answer.
question: Count how many days your last build, measure, learn loop took, and name what slowed it down.
closing_statement: Speed of honest feedback beats speed of shipping.
caption:
Principle Nº 288: Build-Measure-Learn Loop

The team that learns every week will beat the team that learns every month. Every time.

Build something, measure what people actually do, then decide whether to change course or keep going.

Your turn: Count how many days your last build, measure, learn loop took, and name what slowed it down.
